title: introduce-static-egress-nlb-accelerator-and-privatelink-for-control-plane
author: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Adds a new Terraform module and installer hooks to provide deterministic static egress IPs for private control plane traffic using an AWS Network Load Balancer (NLB) + Global Accelerator fronting private ENIs, plus PrivateLink interface endpoints for customer control-plane access. Motivation: Customers deploying Redwood Private want stable outbound IPs for allowlisting in partner systems and on-prem firewalls, and stronger isolation between control plane and tenant data plane. This change implements an opinionated service-network pattern that avoids introducing a Transit Gateway dependency and keeps the control plane reachable via PrivateLink. What this PR does: 1) New module 'control_plane-egress-accelerator' (terraform/modules/control_plane_egress_accelerator) - provisions NLB with IP target groups, Global Accelerator allocation + accelerators in customer region(s) to provide static anycast egress IPs, and optional Elastic IPs for NAT fallback. 2) Adds 'control-plane-privatelink' module to create interface endpoints (AWS::EC2::VPCEndpoint) with endpoint policy templating and per-environment service names. 3) Security hardening - new security groups implementing zero-trust rules: control-plane-internal (only accepts ENI traffic from redwood-data-plane SGs), control-plane-admin (SSH/HTTPS from management CIDRs only). 4) Installer hooks and Helm chart flags - installer/helm-values.yaml includes new keys (egressAccelerator.enabled, privatelink.serviceName, allowedManagementCidrs) and the helm templates wire up endpoint discovery for control-plane components. 5) Upgrade/rollback plan automation - terraform/plans/accelerator-rollout.md and installer scripts include a blue/green rollout pattern: create accelerator and NLB in parallel, add new target group with weight zero, gradually reweight traffic and then switch DNS alias to accelerate cutover; rollback reverses weights and destroys new resources if health checks fail. 6) Reference docs and migration script - tools/migrate/static-egress-migrate.sh helps existing Private deployments opt in with minimal downtime. Migration impact: opt-in; default behavior unchanged unless egressAccelerator.enabled=true. Rollout constraints: customers with Transit Gateway-based topologies must set useTransitGateway=false or follow the migration notes. Testing and CI: included integration test harness updates (test/integration/accelerator) that spin up a small NLB+GA configuration in a sandbox account and verify static IP stability, endpoint connectivity, and security group enforcement. The first CI run uncovered IAM policy issues for the Global Accelerator role; fixed in a follow-up commit. Checklist: [x] Terraform module + vars and outputs [x] Helm chart flag and templates [x] Migration script and docs [x] Integration tests and local test scripts [x] Reviewer feedback addressed Backwards compatibility and safety: This is non-breaking by default; all new infra is behind explicit flags. The PR adds explicit destroy-safe tags for resources created during a rollout to ensure clean rollback. Related work items: ENG-3281 (static egress), INFRA-742 (privatelink for control plane), SUP-905 (customer support request for stable egress IPs). Notes for operators: When enabling, increase monitoring retention for accelerator health checks and ensure cross-account IAM (if partner allowlisting is required) is in place. Security review notes: Endpoint policies default to least-privilege; we included a policy template with allow-by-service-tag and deny-wide-open placeholders that must be reviewed by security before enabling in prod. CI status: final run passing, integration tests green.

feat(terraform): add control_plane_privatelink module with endpoint policy templating
chore(installer): expose egressAccelerator and privatelink flags in helm values
feat(security): create zero-trust SG templates and validator
test(integration): add accelerator integration tests and sandbox harness
fix(iam): correct GA role policy after CI failure
docs: add migration guide and rollout playbook
review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Please split the broad module into smaller files or add clearer submodule docs; the NLB target group health checks need explicit attributes for TLS listeners.
Maya Chen: Addressed by adding health_check blocks and extracting GA config into vars; added examples in terraform/examples/accelerator
Priya Nair: Can we avoid Global Accelerator if customers require single-region deterministic IPs? Suggest adding a flag to select GA vs. EIP-NAT fallback.
Maya Chen: Added egressAccelerator.mode with options [global-accelerator, eip-nat, none] and documented tradeoffs in docs/private/egress-accelerator.md
Carlos Mendez: Integration tests flaked in first CI run due to IAM role propagation; re-run looks good and logging added to test harness
Priya Nair: Security review approved the default endpoint policy template but requests manual approval for production enablement noted in docs
release_notes: Optional: Adds a new opt-in control plane static egress capability backed by NLB + Global Accelerator and PrivateLink interface endpoints. Admins can enable deterministic egress IPs and stronger endpoint isolation. Migration requires enabling egressAccelerator in the installer; follow docs/private/egress-accelerator.md for step-by-step rollout.
